newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to float national pawnshop chain stake.
newsitem.headline: Hungary to float national pawnshop chain stake.

text.p: Hungary will sell a 29 percent stake or a nominal 640 million forints in pawnshop chain BAV Rt in the first half of 1997, and will seek bourse listing later this year, privatisation officials said on Wednesday.
"The privatisation strategy we agreed will maintain BAV's specific national character," Pal Szabo, State Privatisation Agency APV's general director told a news conference.
BAV has 115 shops nationwide, of which one third in Budapest, and beside its pawnshops activity also sells artworks and antiques, as well as used consumer goods. @

APV will sell the 29 percent stake in a private placement on the domestic market, and a public domestic offer of a 32.15 percent stake and subsequent bourse listing will happen this autumn, Szabo said.
Andras Vitezi, BAV's General Director said the company's results made it suitable for privatisation.

"BAV is now finally ready for privatisation," he said, adding that BAV has posted a 460 million to 480 million forints pre-tax profit in 1996 on sales of 6.2 billion forints, compared with a 26 million forints pre-tax profit on sales of 4.3 billion in 1993. @
Figures for 1994 and 1995 were not immediately available.
The company has a registered capital of 2.2 billion forints and shareholders' capital of three billion forints, Vitezi said.
